load_bearing_claims.claim: Cloudera's CFM, CSA and CSM Operator requirement/release-notes pages make no statement about CPU architecture at all; arm64 support for CSO is neither confirmed nor denied by Cloudera, and only the upstream components (Strimzi >=0.27.0, apache/nifi 2.x images, Apache Flink K8s Operator) are documented multi-arch.
load_bearing_claims.why_it_matters: This is the single fact the whole 'CSO operators ON the DGX Spark' plan (ch9-ch12) rests on, and it is unresolved: the guide cannot claim support either way until someone probes container.repository.cloudera.com manifests for arm64 layers (docker manifest inspect / crane) from a session with registry access. Single-sourced by r11 only; the Cloudera multi-arch CI/CD blog that might settle it returned 403.

load_bearing_claims.claim: On GB10 the classic NVIDIA k8s device plugin crashes because nvmlDeviceGetMemoryInfo returns 'Not Supported' under unified memory; the fix is k8s-device-plugin v0.17.4 or newer (whose release note reads 'Ignore errors getting device memory using NVML'), and MIG is unavailable so time-slicing is the only GPU-sharing mechanism.
load_bearing_claims.why_it_matters: Gates whether nvidia.com/gpu capacity ever appears on the k3d/k3s node (ch8/ch9) and whether NiFi/Flink GPU pods can co-exist with an LLM server (no memory isolation). Effectively single-sourced: one blog plus a fetch-tool summary of the release page; the same blog also cites driver 580.95.05/CUDA 12.x, which contradicts NVIDIA's own release notes (580.159.03/CUDA 13.0.2), so verify the v0.17.4 changelog directly and test on the box.

load_bearing_claims.claim: k3d with GPU is not documented on any DGX Spark; k3d's own CUDA guide says the stock k3s node image is Alpine-based, 'the NVIDIA container runtime is not supported on Alpine yet', so a custom CUDA-base node image with runtimeClassName: nvidia is required — whereas plain k3s (--docker or containerd) is proven on real GB10 hardware by multiple sources.
load_bearing_claims.why_it_matters: The plan says 'k3d + Cloudera operators on the box'. Every proven recipe (Collabnix, forum shahizat, rajsinghtechbot, dgxarley) is k3s, not k3d. The guide must either prove k3d's Docker-in-Docker GPU path on unified memory empirically (ch8) or switch the plan to k3s; the NemoClaw #878 nested-k3s cgroup v2 failure is a warning sign for nested setups.

load_bearing_claims.claim: Cloudera AI Inference on-premises entered Technical Preview on 2025-08-07 with Cloudera Data Services 1.5.5, and the 2026-02-09 press release says it is 'now available on-premises, accelerated by NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs, Dynamo-Triton and NIM' — without using the words GA or Technical Preview.
load_bearing_claims.why_it_matters: ch5/ch19/ch20's parity story ('same NIM stack on a Blackwell DGX Spark and on Cloudera on-prem/AWS') depends on whether on-prem CAII is production-supported today; the status is ambiguous across the two Cloudera sources and the CAII auth/API page was never directly fetched (search snippet only).

load_bearing_claims.claim: Realistic single-DGX-Spark interactive decode for 20B-120B MoE models is roughly 45-61 tok/s (llama.cpp: GPT-OSS-120B ~60.6 tok/s, GPT-OSS-20B ~60.9, Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B Q8 ~44.3), dropping to ~40 tok/s at 32K context; dense FP16 models are far slower (Qwen3-32B ~3.5 tok/s on early vLLM) and only speculative decoding pushes small MoE much higher (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4 176.66 tok/s reproduced vs 202.63 claimed).
load_bearing_claims.why_it_matters: The guide's headline tok/s claim (ch4/ch6/ch10 sizing for NiFi->LLM) has a 10x spread across buckets for the same model class depending on engine, version, quant and spec-decode (r02 7.0 vs r06 44.3 vs r08 128-176 for ~30B-A3B MoE; 18.3-75 for Qwen3.8-27B across r06/r07/r08). Publish a dated table with engine+flags, never a single number; the 273 GB/s decode ceiling (r06 Register) is the invariant.

load_bearing_claims.claim: NVIDIA (APAC, 2026-07-14) states a 4-node DGX Spark cluster supports inference on models up to 700B parameters with 'near-linear' scaling for fine-tuning/RL — while independent 4-node GLM-5.2 (744B) deployments measure 23-48 tok/s decode at 250K-655K context, and vLLM tensor-parallel-size 2 across two Sparks is reported unstable.
load_bearing_claims.why_it_matters: ch22 must not repeat the vendor ceiling without the measured counterweights (tonyd2wild 23.0/47.9 tok/s; 0xdfi 42.3 peak; forum GLM-4.7 TP=2 node-drop). NVIDIA publishes no measured NCCL GB/s or multi-node tok/s in its own playbooks (r04), so every multi-Spark number in the guide is community-sourced; note the 700B claim is a tweet, not a doc.
